title: quote-lock v1 conformance vectors
purpose: Hand this to a seller who asks 'will your numbers match mine'. Any language reproducing every case agrees with paid-work-queue on the arithmetic and on the digest.

digest.note: The lock below is pinned as two 32-character halves, not as one 64-character literal, because validate.py refuses any committed file holding 64 hex characters standing alone - a Nano seed looks exactly like that. Concatenate the halves to get the digest.

rounding.rationale: Rounding up by at most one raw favours the seller.
rounding.proof: usd carries exactly 4 decimal places and rate_xno_per_usd exactly 10, so their product has at most 14; scaling by 10**30 leaves an integer number of raw every time. The ceiling is a guarantee for callers who scale differently, not live behaviour here.

cases.name: smallest expressible quote
cases.why: The finest usd and the finest rate the wire format allows; still exact, still non-zero.

cases.name: a float path would lose this
cases.why: Exactly 10**28 raw. A binary floating-point product gives 0.010000000000000002 and corrupts the bottom digits.

cases.name: 1e24 raw, the amount that overflowed minia2a's column
digest agreement on a fixed quote
cases.why: Pins blake2b-32 over the canonical bytes. Recompute the preimage from field_order, digest it, split it in two, and compare.

cases.name: an xrb_ payer settles a nano_ quote
cases.why: nano_ and xrb_ spell the same public key. Comparing the strings refuses a payment that did arrive.

cases.name: a different account is refused
cases.why: Same length, valid checksum, wrong payee.
